page: Amazon Web Services m6id.2xlarge is a general purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with two threads per core. The instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware support includes vector extensions up to AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration instructions including AES and SHA-NI.

A key architectural feature of the m6id family is bundled local instance storage. This server includes a 474 GB NVMe solid-state drive directly attached to the host, offering low-latency scratch space without relying solely on networked block volumes. The instance features a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs configured on this type.

Benchmark results place the m6id.2xlarge solidly within average tiers for its class. The system recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 1653.0 and a multi-core score of 6086.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 11423.46. Memory throughput reached 58.64 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 42.04 GB/sec for writes. In application-focused metrics, it sustained 7.86 million Redis SET operations per second and 10.74 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Notable performance drops occur in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and larger language model inference tasks, such as 7B parameter prompt processing at 15.8 tokens per second, where non-accelerated CPU throughput creates a bottleneck.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the inclusion of local NVMe storage provides high transactional density and eliminates external storage transfer overhead for ephemeral data. The instance is well matched for mid-sized relational and in-memory databases, caching nodes, batch processing, CI/CD pipeline workers, and enterprise web applications that benefit from local high-speed caching.
description: Amazon Web Services m6id.2xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose server powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 32.0 GB of DDR4 system memory at 3 GHz, and an integrated 474 GB local NVMe SSD. It features a 3 Gbps baseline network interface and omits dedicated GPUs. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the server delivers consistent mid-range performance, achieving 11423.46 on PassMark CPU, 6086.0 on Geekbench multi-core, and 7.86 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads. Throughput declines on intensive parallel compression and larger LLM inference workloads. The hardware profile makes it cost-efficient for workloads requiring local low-latency scratch storage, such as database caching, web application serving, backend microservices, and continuous integration pipelines.
